subject: Creativity
title: Punk Rock: Three Chords and the Truth
description: A 60-second lesson on Punk Rock: Three Chords and the Truth.

hook.text: A 1976 fanzine showed three guitar chord diagrams and wrote: 'Now form a band.' Punk's creative manifesto in one image.

buildup.text: By the mid-70s, rock music had become bloated — 20-minute guitar solos, concept albums, capes. Punk said 'enough.'

discovery.text: The Ramones proved you could make thrilling music with minimal skill. Energy and attitude replaced technical mastery.

twist.text: Punk's real revolution wasn't musical — it was cultural. DIY ethics: make your own records, zines, labels.

climax.text: Punk spawned post-punk, new wave, indie rock, and the entire DIY music ecosystem.

punchline.text: Punk proved that creativity doesn't require mastery. Just courage.

quiz.question: What was punk rock's most important cultural contribution beyond music?
options: DIY ethics — make your own records, zines, and labels

details.summary: Punk rock stripped music to its essentials: three chords, raw energy, and authentic expression. By rejecting virtuosity and polish, punk proved that passion and authenticity mattered more than technical skill, democratizing music creation and inspiring generations of DIY artists.
details.whyItMatters: Punk's creative philosophy extends beyond music. Its rejection of gatekeeping and celebration of amateur authenticity influenced art, fashion, publishing, and digital culture.
takeaways: Punk rejected technical virtuosity in favor of raw authenticity
The DIY ethos empowered anyone to create and distribute music
Punk's influence on culture extends far beyond the music genre

faq.question: Did punk musicians really not know how to play?
faq.answer: Some genuinely could not play when they started. Others chose simplicity deliberately. The point was that technical limitation should never prevent someone from creating. Many punk musicians later developed significant skill while maintaining the raw aesthetic.

faq.question: How did punk influence culture beyond music?
faq.answer: Punk's DIY philosophy inspired independent publishing, fashion, art, and eventually internet culture. The idea that you do not need permission or credentials to create and share your work became foundational to blogging, indie gaming, and the creator economy.
